pairs.subject: cost-metering
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/usage.ts:169 The scan lane, the main spend class, is built only from persisted computed Scan rows. A scan whose provider calls failed or timed out and degraded to the `mock` engine (UNMETERED_PROVIDER) carries no tokens and is excluded, so failed-call spend in the scan lane leaves no row, which breaks 'failures are spend'.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/usage.ts:169 Scan-lane rows exist only for successful computed scans, so a failed or timed-out inference that degraded to mock has no row and no failure reason. UsageEvent lanes do carry status, and the period window is owned by one helper (usageWindow) and returned with results (windowSince/windowBefore), so the period half of the technique is met.

src/app/usage/usageCallsPanel.tsx:6 Drill-down from a figure to its calls, with failed calls and unpriced calls listed apart from priced ones. The headline cost equals the per-lane sum by construction (foldLaneCost).

src/lib/db/usage.ts:263 An unknown model is never priced at $0. It becomes 'no estimate', is counted in unpricedCalls/allLanesUnpricedCalls, and the headline reads as a floor. This is a counted floor, not a declared conservative rate (see registryProposal).
src/lib/db/usage.ts:164 Spend is broken down by lane, team and repo, and work with no repo is shown as an explicit last row rather than dropped.

pairs.registryProposal: price-tables requires a declared conservative default rate for unknown models, while unit-classes-are-open prescribes a counted floor for unpriced units. This repo applies the floor discipline to the model axis: unknown model -> null, counted, headline shown as a floor. The standard should say whether a counted 'unpriced floor' meets the 'loud default' rule when no dollar ceiling consumes the figure.

pairs.subject: cost-metering
pairs.evidence: src/lib/integrations/otlp.ts:166 Every `type` of claude_code.token.usage datapoint (input, output, cache read, cache creation) is summed into one undifferentiated `tokens` figure, with no nesting and no counted residual. Spend whose resource has no git.repository is also dropped instead of being stored in an org-scope or unattributed bucket.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/integrations/otlp.ts:166 The datapoint `type` attribute is ignored for token.usage (sessions.ts reads `type` only for lines_of_code), so cache classes are folded at par into tokens.

src/lib/integrations/otlp.ts:122 Cost datapoints with no repo attribute are counted only in the transient 202 receipt and are not persisted, even though the record contract has an `org` scope that could hold them. Unattributed spend is a dropped row, not a stored bucket.

src/app/api/integrations/ingest/route.ts:32 A missing costCents/tokens value becomes a definite 0 ('measured nothing'), not unknown. Invalid records are also filtered at line 68 with no count in the response.

src/lib/integrations/otlp.ts:169 The vendor meter's reported cost is recorded as-is rather than rebuilt from a local rate table. Copilot's cost is reported as unavailable rather than estimated (providers.ts:99).
src/lib/integrations/otlp.ts:73 Received, skipped-by-reason, duplicate and unkeyed counts are returned per export, so a connector that stores nothing is visible.

pairs.subject: cost-metering
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/credits.ts:434 When the debit's idempotency key already exists, consumeScanCredit returns a bare 'charged' (also at line 402) without checking whether that key's refund:<key> row exists. The store cannot tell an open attempt from a closed one, and there is no bounded attempt walk. Closed-key reuse is avoided only because callers mint keys per claim attempt or per UUID.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/credits.ts:434 The refund identity is derived from the debit key (refundKeyFor) and keys are namespaced (scan-job:<id>:<attempt>, scan-hold:<uuid>). But a dedupe hit returns 'already charged' with no open-versus-closed signal and no :r2 walk. The old scan:<scanId> fallback (line 381) remains but is unreachable through reserveScanCredit, which always passes a reservationKey.

src/lib/db/credits.ts:392 An atomic conditional decrement is the hard money gate. Refusals map to a machine-readable 402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS with balance (entitlement.ts:110), distinct from a 404 for a missing org. The free-allowance overshoot is declared and bounded in the doc comment.

src/lib/db/credits.ts:419 Debit and refund rows carry repo, scanId, actor and a typed reason, so a refund joins to its debit. The fields are optional at the db chokepoint but repoFullName is required at the reserveScanCredit wrapper.

src/lib/db/credits.ts:327 The allowance month boundary is computed in one function shared by the entitlement read and the consume write. Credit reconciliation takes the caller's [since, before) window instead of re-deriving one. Rows are append-only and stamp balanceAfter.

src/lib/credit-estimate.ts:63 The monthly estimate is advisory and labelled as an estimate net of allowance. The actual gate charges a known single credit, so it does not depend on the estimate. No estimate-vs-actual loop exists, but no gate reads this estimate.

pairs.registryProposal: reversible-debit-and-settle could recognize caller-minted per-attempt keys (job attempt counter, fresh UUID per hold) as a partial substitute for the store-side closed-attempt walk, and state whether that alone is enough.
